title: Acts 17:28
paragraphs: “For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.” — KJV
Brother, this verse hits like thunder wrapped in mercy.

Paul is telling Athens: You are not self-made.
Not self-sustained.
Not self-owned.

In Him you breathe.
In Him you stand.
In Him your next heartbeat is possible.

That means pride has to bow.
But despair has to bow too.

Because if your life is held in God’s hands, then your story is not random. You are not floating through chaos unseen. Even in rebellion, even in confusion, even in a city full of idols, Paul points people back to the God who is near, not far.
But here is what we must not miss:

Acts 17:28 is not saying everyone is automatically saved.
It is saying every human being depends on God completely.
And that reality should lead us to repentance and faith in Christ.
A few verses later, Paul calls all people everywhere to repent because God has appointed a day of judgment through the risen Jesus. So the verse is beautiful, yes—but it is also a wake-up call.

You live because of Him.
Now the question is:

Jesus is not just the source of life.
He is the Savior who rescues ruined lives.
The One who died for sinners.
The One who rose again.
The One who gives meaning, forgiveness, and a future.

Acts 17:28 in one line:
You are alive by God’s power, and you are called to return to God through Christ.
